title: World-Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Pollution-Aware Bird Movement Modeling Using a Multi-Instance DQN Framework
author: Shivin Mangal, Divyansh Chawla, Anshu Garg, Isshaan Singh
contentSnippet: arXiv:2611.21895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Birds are modeled as environmentally sensitive agents whose movement reflects real-world air quality conditions, where AQI serves as a measurable world feedback signal representing pollution-driven consequences. Instead of relying on human preference or synthetic rewards, the system uses environmental outcomes as the primary training signal, enabling policy learning grounded in ecological impact. We propose a multi-instance reinforcement learning simulation in which agents navigate a 2D grid representation of India integrated with a precomputed AQI matrix and geographic state boundaries. The framework combines bird call metadata from the Xeno-canto dataset, spatial discretization, and real environmental data to learn adaptive navigation strategies under pollution constraints. To ensure scalability and efficiency, repeated real-time API queries are replaced by a structured AQI mapping that enables fast lookup during training and execution. Multiple baselines, including Monte Carlo, Q-Learning, and Value Iteration, are evaluated for comparison. Deep Q-Network demonstrates stronger stability, adaptability, and cumulative performance across varying environmental conditions, establishing a scalable foundation for world-feedback driven ecological decision modeling.

title: HypoLoop: Revising Weight-Editing Plans from Scientific Feedback
author: Mengran Li
contentSnippet: Scientific experiments continually reveal prediction errors. Effective updates depend on which parameters change and which errors drive the correction. We introduce HypoLoop, a family of native weight-editing methods that connects these choices to experimental feedback. Fixed, numerically adaptive, and LLM-guided policies produce editing plans; numerical solvers compute weight patches, and internal validation selects the deployed predictor. Successive observations and validation records support revisions to editable locations and fitting rules. Experiments cover 22 scientific tasks and both DeepSeek and Claude. On Burgers, reallocating a matched parameter budget reduces error by 58.80% and 47.72% relative to fixed locations. On DIODE, positive-residual weighting reduces absolute relative error (AbsRel) by 13.35% in internal cross-validation, with the same 33 editable coordinates. Revising the complete plan across rounds lowers final AbsRel by 10.59% relative to keeping the initial plan fixed. SpaceNet7 and Make3D connect accepted edits to improved spatial predictions. These results show how experimental evidence can shape the update problem itself. Code: https://github.com/limengran98/HypoLoop.

title: Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future  deals in doubt
author: Dominic-Madori Davis, Marina Temkin
contentSnippet:
Nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: it revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday , up from the $22 billion reported in January. The increase includes both new investments and significant markups of existing portfolio companies.

The company invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it said, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year. This amount includes buying shares in public and private companies, yet it shows how the chipmaker made massive bets over the course of the year, especially compared to last year ; in November 2025, the company reported spending $5 billion buying equity in the first nine months of that fiscal year.

But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor.

Nvidia stated in late 2023 that the goal of its corporate investing is to expand the AI ecosystem by backing startups it considers to be “game changers and market makers.” Over the nearly three years that followed, the chipmaker has invested in nearly 350 startups, according to PitchBook. The companies Nvidia backed include Anthropic, OpenAI; neolabs like Thinking Machines and Reflection; neoclouds, like Lambda, Nscale, and Crusoe; as well as other companies developing AI infrastructure, robotics startups, and applications.

It’s also become a big financier of the data center build out, reporting $118 billion in guarantees with $105 billion of that the backstop it supplied for OpenAI’s $500 billion data center in Ohio.

The company made those commitments by allocating a meaningful portion of its excess cash flows. In Tuesday’s earning call, Kress said Nvidia would continue providing financing assistance to strong customers and that “as the market matures and additional sources of capital become available,” the company would be “rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees.”

But the question for the VC ecosystem is whether the company will continue to back startups at anywhere near the same level without Huang at the helm.

Huang’s rampant dealmaking has reportedly been a source of concern for Kress. Investors have told TechCrunch that they anticipate that she will take a more conservative approach to startup investing, becoming more selective with new investments and writing smaller-sized checks into its existing portfolio companies.

title: JEV vs. LLMs: A Comparative Analysis for Phishing Email Detection
author: Muhammad Mahir Malik
contentSnippet: Phishing remains a major source of credential theft and fraudulent payments, and email security systems must classify large message volumes reliably, quickly, and at manageable cost. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer flexible text understanding, but their token-based generation increases response time and API cost, and the reliability of their confidence values requires measurement. Jev 1.13, a typed decision model from TypeSafe AI, instead returns a structured outcome with a confidence value. This paper compares Jev 1.13 with Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, and Meta Llama 4 Maverick on a labelled dataset of 1500 emails, covering classification performance, decision latency, token consumption, API cost, and probability calibration. Jev achieves the highest accuracy (79.67%), precision (71.43%), recall (97.97%), and F1 score (82.62%). It also records the shortest batch time (173.88 seconds), the lowest token count (597,895), the lowest cost (USD 0.015103 per 1000 decisions), and the lowest Brier score (0.1698) and ECE (0.1594). These results suggest that Jev is a promising option for fast, structured, high-volume triage. LLMs retain the advantage of generating explanations, which we do not evaluate, and all four systems require further validation before standalone deployment.

title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
author: Julie Bort
contentSnippet:
Despite the turmoil at Nvidia following the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang , the company — as expected — delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday. More importantly, Nvidia reassured investors that its streak of record-breaking revenue won’t stop.

On Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the year-ago quarter and a beat above the company’s guidance. Nvidia had told Wall Street to expect $108 billion in revenue for its third quarter of fiscal 2027. Kress also projected an even bigger fourth quarter, with revenue expected to reach $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.

She also said full-year revenue is on track to exceed expectations.

“We are raising our fiscal year 2028 outlook. We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% and off what is now a higher fiscal 2027 base,” Kress said on the quarterly conference call on Tuesday. “Our outlook considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital.”

The company also reminded investors that it was using some of its billions in cash to buy back shares. In September 2026, Nvidia increased its share buyback program by $150 billion. It spent $28.1 billion on its own shares during the quarter and still had another $227.3 billion remaining in the kitty for additional repurchases.

Ironically, Nvidia could also benefit from the plunge in its share price following Huang’s resignation last week, should shares remain depressed over the longer term. The stock is down about 10% since his departure. Investors, however, celebrated Tuesday’s quarterly results, sending shares up about 4% in after-hours trading.

Kress stressed that the company was in good shape now and for the foreseeable future, even without Huang at the helm.

“We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress stressed. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.”

She added that the company has secured memory and advanced packaging capacity and is working with its chip manufacturer, TSMC, to “narrow the supply and demand gaps.”

Financially, Nvidia continues to leverage its cash reserves for aggressive share repurchases. title: HINT-WAM: Hindsight-Informed Training for World Action Models
author: Phuong Tuan Dat, Qi Li, Xinchao Wang
contentSnippet: World action models (WAMs) have shown promising generalization and data efficiency in robot manipulation by coupling action generation with predictions of future visual dynamics. Translating these capabilities into reliable task execution, however, remains a challenge for existing post-training methods. Offline supervised fine-tuning provides dense supervision on expert trajectories, but its flow-matching action expert is trained only on noised demonstration actions and never on the intermediate states produced by its own sampler; task-specific adaptation can also compromise pretrained capabilities. On-policy reinforcement learning trains on the policy's own behavior, yet sparse task rewards make exploration and credit assignment difficult, while dense reward shaping still provides scalar evaluations rather than direct action targets. We introduce HINT-WAM, the first on-policy self-distillation framework that supervises the action expert on its own sampling trajectories using hindsight, the future video of the demonstration, as privileged information available to the WAM itself. For each demonstration observation, the student generates its action through its own denoising trajectory, and at the states along this trajectory the same model acts as a teacher conditioned additionally on this hindsight, providing a conditional action distribution as a dense training target, while the student sees only deployment-time inputs and needs no environmental rewards or simulator interaction. To transfer this supervision to a flow-matching action expert, HINT-WAM distills the teacher into the student with an energy score, a distribution-level objective that matches the teacher's action distribution from the student's own samples rather than regressing its velocity field. The project web is available in https://tuandattt.github.io/hintwam/.

summary.tldr:
Researchers have introduced HINT-WAM (Hindsight-Informed Training for World Action Models), a novel on-policy self-distillation framework designed to improve robot manipulation by addressing the limitations of offline supervised fine-tuning and traditional reinforcement learning. While existing methods often suffer from distribution shift—where the action expert is trained on expert trajectories but fails to handle the intermediate states generated by its own sampler—HINT-WAM enables the model to supervise its own action generation process. By utilizing 'hindsight' (the future video of a demonstration) as privileged information, the framework allows the model to act as both student and teacher, providing dense action targets without requiring environmental rewards or simulator interaction.

The technical core of HINT-WAM involves a flow-matching action expert that is distilled using an energy-score objective. During training, the student generates actions through its own denoising trajectory while the teacher, conditioned on the hindsight video, provides a conditional action distribution. Instead of regressing the velocity field, the framework uses a distribution-level objective to match the teacher's action distribution based on the student's own samples. This approach allows the model to learn from its own behavior while maintaining the generalization capabilities of the pretrained World Action Model, effectively bridging the gap between demonstration-based training and reliable task execution.
takeaways: **Framework Mechanism:** HINT-WAM uses on-policy self-distillation where the model acts as both student (deployment-time inputs) and teacher (conditioned on hindsight video).
**Objective Function:** The method employs an energy-score objective to match action distributions rather than regressing the velocity field of the flow-matching expert.
**Data Efficiency:** The framework eliminates the need for environmental rewards or simulator interaction by leveraging privileged hindsight information from demonstration trajectories.

**Problem Addressed:** The approach mitigates distribution shift inherent in offline supervised fine-tuning, where models are trained on expert data but fail to generalize to their own generated intermediate states.

title: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
author: Zhenqing Ling, Qirui Jiao, Daoyuan Chen, Cheng Chen
contentSnippet:
Authors: Zhenqing Ling , Qirui Jiao , Daoyuan Chen , Cheng Chen , Xinji Mai , Haowen Gao , Zhuo Zhang , Xuchen Pan , Mengsu Ding , Jiaji Deng , Yuexiang Xie , Xiaoming Qin , Weirui Kuang , Zhaoyang Liu , Yaliang Li , Bolin Ding , Jingren Zhou

Abstract: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). The models predict probabilities over candidate answers for general-purpose text and visual judgments, agent harnesses, data workflows, and interactive games. Piccolo-27B tops the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard with a score of 75.59, while Piccolo-9B and Piccolo-4B achieve 68.35 and 67.46, respectively. All three rank first on the Private benchmark in their respective model-size categories. Research agents analyze model behavior, construct training data, conduct experiments, and use the results to refine subsequent proposals. Semantic slices and a shared research memory connect these actions across the model family's development. With training recipes comprising hundreds of thousands of examples, data selection and feedback-driven refinement are central to the self-improvement process. Our large-scale RSI exploration yields three counter-intuitive insights for decision-model development: (1) Backbone-recipe co-adaptation outweighs raw model recency: earlier backbones can surpass newer generations on visual tasks under identical recipes; (2) Targeted data curation enables 4B-9B models to rival 27B baselines on specialized workflows; and (3) Continuous loss reduction can decouple from and even degrade discrete decision accuracy. Together with the released weights and tools from the Data-Juicer and AgentScope ecosystems, Piccolo provides an actionable blueprint for building frontier decision models and scaling data-driven RSI.

Notes: 22 pages, 13 figures, 11 tables. Project page and blog: this https URL

summary.tldr:
A research team led by Jingren Zhou and colleagues from Alibaba Group has introduced Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models ranging from 0.8B to 27B parameters. Designed for general-purpose text and visual judgments, agent harnesses, data workflows, and interactive games, the models utilize a methodology called Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). This process employs research agents to analyze model behavior, generate training data, and conduct iterative experiments, supported by a shared research memory and semantic slicing to refine model development across the family.

Performance metrics highlight the 27B model achieving a score of 75.59 on the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard, while the 9B and 4B variants secured scores of 68.35 and 67.46, respectively, each ranking first in their size categories on the Private benchmark. The research identifies three key findings: backbone-recipe co-adaptation is more critical than model recency for visual tasks; targeted data curation allows smaller 4B-9B models to match 27B baselines in specialized workflows; and continuous loss reduction does not always correlate with, and can sometimes degrade, discrete decision accuracy. The project includes released weights and tools integrated with the Data-Juicer and AgentScope ecosystems.
takeaways: **Model Performance:** Piccolo-27B leads the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard with a 75.59 score, while 9B and 4B models top their respective size categories on the Private benchmark.
**Methodology:** The models are developed using Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI), where research agents autonomously construct training data and refine proposals.

**Counter-intuitive Findings:** The study concludes that backbone-recipe co-adaptation is more impactful than model recency, and that continuous loss reduction can negatively impact discrete decision accuracy.
**Ecosystem Integration:** The project provides open weights and tools compatible with the existing Data-Juicer and AgentScope frameworks.
**Scale:** The research encompasses a model family spanning 0.8B to 27B parameters, supported by training recipes consisting of hundreds of thousands of examples.

title: Movie2Game-Bench: Holistic Evaluation of Film-to-Game Adaptation Beyond Playability
author: Jialing Xie, Yifan Zhou, Yiwen Zhang, Junjun He
contentSnippet: Adapting a film into a game requires selecting source elements and translating them into player actions, rules, and feedback. We introduce Movie2Game-Bench (M2G-bench), a benchmark for evaluating film-to-game adaptation beyond playability. M2G-bench combines general evaluation, movie-specific evaluation, and playtesting by three GUI model players. The protocol connects source content to gameplay steps and implementation evidence, capturing both content preservation and interactive realization. The benchmark comprises 22 films and 658 source-specific reference items. Evaluating 14 models on the same films with their selected primary harnesses reveals complementary strengths in game quality, adaptation, and player experience. A shared weakness concerns playable sequences: this category has the lowest content-presence mean in all 14 models, averaging 37.9 out of 100 compared with 54.8 for iconic elements. Among judgments of retained emotionaldevelopment content, narrative choices account for 60.0% and scenario operation for 7.2%. These findings identify two linked priorities for film-to-game adaptation: preserving source situations that can support gameplay and connecting retained content to player actions and consequences.

title: UltraTex: Aligning Physical Knowledge for High-Fidelity PBR Texture Generation
author: Jingzhi Bao, Xiaohe Ma, Hong Li, Yuanming Hu
contentSnippet: Generating physically based rendering (PBR) texture maps for a 3D mesh from a single reference image is highly ambiguous, as the observed appearance entangles material identity, surface reflectance, and illumination. While current generative methods produce realistic albedo maps, they still struggle to infer accurate metallic and roughness attributes for relighting. We present UltraTex, a cascaded multi-view framework that moves beyond appearance matching by integrating physical knowledge into multi-view diffusion-based PBR generation. UltraTex first jointly predicts albedo and world-space shading normals to generate more detailed albedo maps, and then predicts metallic-roughness (MR) maps conditioned on the generated albedo, reference image, and material semantic priors. To inject material semantics, a lightweight adapter transforms hidden-layer features of a vision-language model (VLM) into intrinsic material representation tokens, providing part-level knowledge anchors for MR estimation. To model material-light interaction, photometric representation alignment guides intermediate diffusion features toward ground-truth material renderings under controlled lighting. This makes metallic and roughness variations observable through highlight intensity, specular sharpness, and local reflectance contrast, providing stronger guidance for fine-grained material prediction without explicit lighting supervision. Extensive experiments show that UltraTex generates high-quality textures and outperforms existing open-source and commercial methods in visual fidelity, material accuracy, and physical plausibility.

title: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents
author: Lipeng He, Yihan Wang, Jiawen Zhang, N. Asokan
contentSnippet: Large language model (LLM) agents routinely interact with untrusted external data, exposing them to indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks that hijack agents into executing attacker-chosen tasks. To uncover these vulnerabilities at scale, automated red-teaming methods often leverage reinforcement learning (RL) to generate attacks that achieve high attack success rates (ASR). Model developers use the attacks discovered during internal red-teaming to harden agents through adversarial training before deployment, a collaborative offensive-defensive process known in cybersecurity as purple-teaming. However, we show that achieving high ASR during red-teaming does not guarantee robustness gains from subsequent adversarial training. Specifically, we find that two state-of-the-art RL-based red-teaming methods, RL-Hammer and PISmith, suffer from mode collapse, repeatedly discovering similar attack strategies whose additional successes add no additional robustness improvements to adversarial training. To address this gap, we introduce PIPETTE, a unified prompt injection purple-teaming framework that effectively converts red-teaming discoveries into defender robustness improvements. PIPETTE employs a dictionary learning-based reward that encourages broader coverage of attack strategies during red-teaming. It also integrates an on-policy adversarial training pipeline tailored to IPI defense, enabling agents to resist attacks while completing legitimate user tasks. Extensive evaluations across agentic benchmarks (AgentDojo and ASB) demonstrate that PIPETTE produces defenders that achieve near-zero attack success rates on static attacks and can withstand strong adaptive attacks, while maintaining benign task utility close to that of the undefended baseline.

title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
author: Mingliang Zhai, Chuanhao Li, Jiaming Tan, Zhen Li
contentSnippet: Rules govern how player actions change interactive worlds. Different rules create distinct gameplay experiences within similar scenes and action spaces. For customizable gameplay, generative world models must follow user-defined rules beyond real-world behaviors. However, realizing user-defined rules presents two challenges: Rule-State Persistence and Rule-to-Visual Realization. The former requires preserving rule definitions, dependencies, and world states across saving and loading, so that restored worlds follow the established rules. The latter requires accurately realizing rule-induced changes on designated objects and attributes, particularly when affected objects are unseen. In this paper, we propose WorldRuler, which organizes rule definitions, dependencies, and object states in an executable 3D rule graph and connects rule execution, video generation, and perceptual feedback in a closed loop. The graph supports joint saving and restoration of rules and world states, while dynamic object binding grounds rule-specified entities in visual instances and uses stored states to constrain generation from their first appearance. We further introduce object attribute state replacement and counterfactual reconstruction training, enabling accurate attribute control and compatible appearance and motion changes while limiting interference with unrelated content. We develop an automated data collection and annotation pipeline using GTA-V and Habitat to construct RuleVerse, a dataset of rule-driven interactions with detailed state and event annotations, including cases where rules take effect before affected objects become visible. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of WorldRuler in preserving rule-state consistency across saving and loading and accurately realizing rule outcomes on designated objects and attributes.

title: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards
author: Yeongtak Oh, Donghyeok Lee, Joonhee Oh, Jaewon Jeong
contentSnippet: Personalized vision-language assistants use visual observations and personal memories to provide advice tailored to the user. When the observed scene contains a physical hazard, personal context, such as allergies, medical conditions, or mobility constraints, can change what help is appropriate. Responding appropriately therefore requires recognizing the visible hazard and applying the relevant person's information. We introduce PReMind-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark that evaluates this combination across diverse hazards and personal-memory conditions. It separately measures memory access, grounding, abstention, and hazard response, and assesses joint success on interdependency cases. Existing models often satisfy one requirement while failing the other, and training only for safety or personalization leaves a gap in joint success. We therefore propose PReMind, a two-phase reinforcement learning framework that combines on-demand and forced-call interactions (memory always retrieved) to jointly train grounded memory use and hazard response. At 4B, PReMind raises joint success from 12.9% to 28.6% over its base on the interdependency set and improves hazard adequacy and correct abstention on the main test. Joint-success gains persist under forced-call evaluation and under a second LLM judge across three Phase II seeds; averaged over these seeds, joint success also improves on unseen hazard groups. These findings highlight the need to evaluate and train personal assistants to connect visual evidence with the relevant person's context.

title: Late Entry in Looped Language Models
author: Ziqi Jin, Jiaxi Li, Weiwen Xu, Aixin Sun
contentSnippet: Looped language models deepen reasoning at a compact parameter count by iterating a shared layer stack T times per token, turning recurrence depth directly into sequential decoding latency. Conventional early-exit decoding halts after initial passes without cache completion, truncating cached key-value states of past tokens to shallow depth. We study the opposite strategy, late entry, where new tokens skip initial passes and enter directly into the final K T alongside subsequent steps at zero extra serial calls. Projecting these finished T-pass wake states inside the existing output GEMM (Wake verification, governed by logit-margin tolerance tau in [0, inf]) unifies greedy-exact T-pass decoding (tau = 0, matching K = T block decoding within bf16 reduction order), margin-gated verification (tau > 0), and non-rollback lossy late entry (tau = inf) inside a single static CUDA graph. On Ouro-2.6B (T = 4), K = 2 Wake reaches 5.2x greedy-exact speedup at tau = 0 (+26% over K = 4 block decoding on GSM8K) and 6.8x at tau = inf (+16.9 points over trained early exit at matched speed). Scaling test-time recurrence across T in {8, 16, 32, 64} on Huginn-3.5B cuts K = T/4 rollbacks 21.5x with depth, driving greedy-exact (tau = 0) speedups to 6.1x (T = 32) and 8.4x (T = 64, +153% over K = 64 block) and tau = inf speedups to 10.6 to 12.5x.

Looped language models deepen reasoning at a compact parameter count by iterating a shared layer stack T times per token, turning recurrence depth directly into sequential decoding latency. We study the opposite strategy, late entry, where new tokens skip initial passes and enter directly into the final K T alongside subsequent steps at zero extra serial calls.

Projecting these finished T-pass wake states inside the existing output GEMM (Wake verification, governed by logit-margin tolerance tau in [0, inf]) unifies greedy-exact T-pass decoding (tau = 0, matching K = T block decoding within bf16 reduction order), margin-gated verification (tau > 0), and non-rollback lossy late entry (tau = inf) inside a single static CUDA graph. On Ouro-2.6B (T = 4), K = 2 Wake reaches 5.2x greedy-exact speedup at tau = 0 (+26% over K = 4 block decoding on GSM8K) and 6.8x at tau = inf (+16.9 points over trained early exit at matched speed). Scaling test-time recurrence across T in {8, 16, 32, 64} on Huginn-3.5B cuts K = T/4 rollbacks 21.5x with depth, driving greedy-exact (tau = 0) speedups to 6.1x (T = 32) and 8.4x (T = 64, +153% over K = 64 block) and tau = inf speedups to 10.6 to 12.5x.

title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
author: Ruisi Zhao, You Li, Sihan Chen, Aosong Cheng
contentSnippet: Video rough-cut is a core stage in media production workflows, organizing raw media materials into an initial video cut. Despite recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) for video-related tasks, automatic rough-cut remains underexplored, without a comprehensive benchmark for evaluation or mature workflows for producing executable cut plans. To address the evaluation gap, we introduce RoughCut-Bench, which covers two practical settings: (1) a visually driven setting over video cases, covering highlight detection and selection, source-video ordering, and adherence to user requirements when provided; and (2) a speech-driven setting over automatic speech recognition (ASR) transcripts, covering filler removal, expression deduplication, and low-value content trimming. Across these settings, the benchmark contains 101 visually driven cases, including 831 raw videos with 1,476 highlight annotations. It also includes 84 speech-driven cases, each consisting of an ASR transcript with annotated cleanup spans. The evaluation compares cut plans with these annotations in both settings and additionally uses a human-aligned agentic evaluator to assess rendered-cut quality in the visual setting. To apply LVLMs to automatic rough-cut, we further propose agentic workflows that guide them to produce structured cut plans from input materials. Experiments show that current LVLMs remain limited in producing expert-aligned cut plans. Our benchmark, code, and prompts are released at https://whalesong-zrs.github.io/RoughCut-Bench-Project-Page.

title: DrawScore: Evaluating Generated CAD Models against Engineering Drawings
author: Haorui Chen, Shiteng Lu, Zhanyu Guo, Zaixi Li
contentSnippet: Automatic CAD generation is commonly evaluated with volumetric IoU, Chamfer Distance, and surface F-score, which barely penalize local errors that occupy only a small fraction of a part's volume or surface area, such as a misplaced hole or a slot on the wrong face, even though such errors are critical to manufacturing. We formalize these metrics in a unified integral form and show that the weight of a local error decays as the (k+q)-th power of its size, where k is the dimension of the integration domain and q is determined by the penalty function. Guided by this analysis, we propose DrawScore, which projects both models into three orthographic views with visible and hidden lines, as in engineering drawings, and applies a saturating penalty along the projected curves, so that the weight of a local error decays only linearly. Controlled experiments confirm the predicted decay orders, and on outputs of existing CAD generation agents, DrawScore exposes errors in outputs that IoU rates as nearly perfect. DrawScore further improves generation as a reinforcement learning reward and, for CAD generation from engineering drawings, serves as a test-time verifier without 3D ground truth or an additional reward model. Our code is available at https://github.com/UESTC-Simon/DrawScore.

title: Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models
author: Wen Wang, Jindong Wang, Jiahua Bao, Tu Yongsiqi
contentSnippet: Reinforcement learning from terminal answer rewards enables search-augmented language models to interleave reasoning and retrieval without step-level annotations, yet outcome supervision assigns identical credit to every search in a trajectory regardless of whether it retrieved useful information. This limitation is especially severe when all sampled rollouts for a question fail, collapsing group-centered outcome advantages to zero even when trajectories gather markedly different evidence. We present Evidence-based Credit Assignment (ECA), which augments terminal outcome rewards with a training-only auxiliary signal measuring how retrieved documents improve the likelihood of a reference answer. Rather than scoring the full dialogue prefix, ECA queries a frozen snapshot of the current policy under an evidence-only prompt containing solely the question and the deduplicated documents observed so far, isolating the utility of retrieved passages from surface variations in generated thoughts or search queries. Within this framework, we compare two return formulations, ECA-Step (which accumulates step-clipped potential increments) and ECA-Horizon (which preserves the telescoping horizon gain in potential), paired with cross-fold group normalization, novelty gating, and search-local token assignment. Across seven Search QA benchmarks, ECA-Horizon improves strict macro exact match over an outcome-only GRPO baseline by 1.03 and 4.80 percentage points on Qwen2.5-3B- and 7B-Instruct, respectively, outperforming both RLOO and GiGPO. Zero-shot evaluation on MultiHop-RAG further demonstrates strong transfer to multi-hop inference queries.

title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
author: Haoran Ye, Tianrui Huo, Hangzhen Li, Xin Zhang
contentSnippet: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to infer psychological attributes, predict individual behaviour, and simulate human populations. However, despite generating plausible responses, they often misrepresent individuals and distort population statistics. Here we introduce Chiron, a foundation model to measure and predict human behaviour. We jointly fine-tune an LLM to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align population response distributions with human statistics. The training and evaluation data span 36 behavioural domains and 78 social science experiments, comprising 288,307 person records, 1,411,750 atomic behavioural decisions, and 99,953 psychometric assessments over 109 psychological constructs. In our evaluations, Chiron's psychological measurements agree more closely with human self-reports and exhibit fewer biases that undermine psychometric validity. It predicts individual behaviour more accurately than frontier LLMs (up to 28.4% relative improvement). In simulations of social science experiments, it more accurately captures the direction and magnitude of human experimental effects (82.2--94.3% lower effect-size estimation error). Together, these results establish Chiron as a unified computational instrument for measuring and predicting human behaviour.

title: Mechanistic Critics for Sample-Efficient NPU Design-Space Exploration
author: Yicheng He, Yuqi Xue, Tianyang Wu, Jian Huang
contentSnippet: NPU design-space exploration for LLM inference mainly relies on an expensive simulator that often returns only scalar feedback such as latency and power. Such feedback can rank evaluated configurations, but gives little information for deciding why a configuration is slow or which architecture parameter should be changed next. This limitation is especially severe because prefill and decode workloads can be limited by different resources, including compute throughput and HBM bandwidth. We propose CriticNPU, a sample-efficient DSE framework built around an online-calibrated mechanistic critic for NPU architecture design. The critic uses explicit hardware limits to evaluate NPU configurations: before simulation, it estimates whether a proposed configuration is likely to improve over the current best and filters weak candidates; after simulation, it aggregates operator-level runtimes into prefill/decode bottleneck summaries and predicts the effect of candidate parameter changes. We instantiate the critic with a Roofline-style model that derives compute and memory limits from architecture parameters and calibrates per-operator-type effective limits using simulator observations. And CriticNPU combines this critic with a workload extractor and an architecture planner to propose configurations. Across six LLM workloads and 16 deployment configurations per model, CriticNPU achieves best-or-tied-best latency in 74% of prefill and 87.5% of decode settings while using roughly half the simulator calls of competitive DSE baselines. We conduct extensive ablation studies and detailed analyses to validate the effectiveness of our method from multiple perspectives. Our code is available at https://github.com/bruno686/CriticNPU.

title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
author: Yuhe Liu, Qi Li, Shihua Zhang, Xinchao Wang
contentSnippet: System One models such as Jev return decisions through fast, parallel prediction. In this paper, we introduce Jeveration, showing that the same decision paradigm can also generate high-quality images in a single forward pass. Jeveration builds on a frozen vision-language model, repurposing its visual-semantic knowledge for holistic image generation. The key challenge is to maintain global consistency. A single prompt admits many valid images, yet parallel predictions must converge on a coherent whole. We therefore condition all positions on a shared random state to coordinate parallel predictions, so that each draw yields a different but coherent image. Since the model tends to ignore this state under direct image supervision, we first learn a distribution over discrete image codes to guide single-pass generation. Beyond text-to-image generation, we further unify image-to-image generation and dense prediction within the same architecture, so that one checkpoint supports all three tasks, each in one forward pass. Experiments show that Jeveration generates a 512x512 image in 78 ms, up to 122x faster than existing unified models, while maintaining competitive image quality and dense prediction performance.

title: WaveView: The Novel View Is in the Noise
author: Kaiwen Wang, Jan-Hendrik Pauls, Yinzhe Shen, Frank Bieder
contentSnippet: Generative novel view synthesis (NVS) employs a diffusion model to render a static or dynamic scene from a target camera view. Explicit warp methods complete a reprojection of the source with video diffusion models, and implicit methods encode the camera parameters or 3D cues. Both add inference overhead, and the generated layout often drifts from the ground truth. We present WaveView, which injects the warped source into the phase of the initial noise of a pretrained generator. The Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Packet Transform (DT-CWPT) allows local and anisotropic phase injection. The generator is thus constrained less in disoccluded regions and along the epipolar line. WaveView keeps the architecture and adds negligible overhead. On the DL3DV benchmark, it outperforms all baselines in every overlap bin. In the hardest bin, it gains 0.84 dB PSNR on the covisible region over MetaView, which shares its generator, while running 2.1 times faster. For dynamic NVS, fine-tuning AnyView with the same noise raises its zero-shot PSNR on AnyViewBench from 11.58 to 12.35 dB.

title: StrideWorld: Benchmarking Scene Rigidity and Action Consistency in Interactive Video World Model
author: Chuang Wang, Rui Nie, Jie Song, Junyuan Gao
contentSnippet: Interactive video world models turn user commands into the exploration of a generated scene, which requires the scene to keep its 3D structure as the camera moves and each action to keep a stable effect. Existing benchmarks mostly evaluate these properties against references fitted to the video under test, either a scene reconstructed from its own frames or a camera trajectory aligned to the command path with a free scale. Such references can absorb gradual scene deformation and changes in pace and route length, so these errors can pass undetected. We therefore introduce StrideWorld, a benchmark whose references are fixed before the motion they judge. It evaluates scene rigidity against the ground-truth geometry of the start view, and action consistency against the stride of each action, the camera motion of one command. The stride is measured on the model's first steps and then used to test the steps that follow, so each model is judged only against its own steps. Its measurements are validated on rendered videos with known camera motion, and its scores agree with human judgments. Across videos generated by open models from 140 start views, all models but one deform their scenes as the camera moves, with offsets up to 7.3 times those of a rigid rendering along the same camera path. Most models keep a steady pace when a single action is held. Along composed routes, several models often stall, and most completed routes end away from the positions predicted by each model's own strides. Only the two models that scale commands by the estimated scene depth bring most routes close to these positions. Fine-tuning two models on a few rendered clips removes most of their mid-route stalls. Code, data, and a leaderboard are publicly available at https://github.com/chuangwang123/strideworld.

title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
author: Rui Li, Liyang He, Zheng Zhang, Zhenya Huang
contentSnippet: Autonomous LLM agents incur substantial cost and latency by invoking a large model (System-2) at every step, even when many intermediate actions choose among a small set of known candidates. Existing dual-system agents offload such decisions to a lightweight System-1 model, but rely on workflow-specific hooks authored per environment. We present AnyS1, a framework that turns human-authored procedural skills, whose instructions naturally specify where choices arise and which options apply, into a shared, domain-general source of decision points. Offline, AnyS1 mines grounded enumerable decisions across over 1,000 public skills, gathers execution-grounded trajectory states inside isolated containers to construct Any-DP, and trains a single calibrated 4B pointer System-1 with label smoothing. At run time, compiled workflows resolve routine decisions in one forward pass and fall back to System-2 when confidence falls below a calibrated threshold. Across three unseen benchmarks and distinct System-2 model families, AnyS1 preserves task reliability while cutting episode cost by 75-91% and model-call time by 63-92% relative to an uncompiled System-2 agent, and maintains performance under zero-shot threshold transfer.

title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
author: Zeguan Xiao, Zhuocheng Liang, Yun Chen, Yong Wang
contentSnippet: A central challenge in adapting large language models (LLMs) is capability preservation: an adaptation can achieve its target while degrading general capabilities. We introduce CurvDelta, a scalable framework that incorporates the preservation constraint into the parameterization of the model update. By analyzing the local geometry of the preservation constraint around the pre-adaptation model, CurvDelta constructs a low-curvature space in which parameter updates leave the preservation loss nearly invariant. We make its construction practical for LLMs through Kronecker-factored approximate curvature (K-FAC) and a factorized projection. We also introduce CurvLoRA, a low-rank variant within the same preservation geometry, designed for more efficient adaptation. Both methods apply to preservation-constrained adaptation tasks such as capability learning and selective unlearning. We evaluate our methods on mathematical reasoning, code generation, and knowledge unlearning. For mathematical reasoning and code generation, our approaches achieve competitive downstream performance while better preserving general capabilities, offering a favorable acquisition--retention trade-off relative to the baselines. For knowledge unlearning, our main results on TOFU and MUSE show a better balance between targeted forgetting and knowledge retention than the baselines, with retention performance close to the from-scratch retraining reference.

title: Alphabet’s Isomorphic Labs raises $5B to accelerate drug discovery with AI
author: Maria Deutscher
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 18:51 EST / NOVEMBER 17 2026

Alphabet’s Isomorphic Labs raises $5B to accelerate drug discovery with AI

Isomorphic Labs Ltd. today announced that it has closed a $5 billion investment led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital.

The venture capital firms were joined by more than a half-dozen other backers. The group included Isomorphic parent Alphabet Inc., which made a “significant investment.” The search giant provided the capital through its GV and CapitalG startup funds.

Isomorphic offers a software platform called the Isomorphic Labs Drug Design Engine, or IsoDDE for short. It uses artificial intelligence to speed up several of the tasks involved in developing new medicines. The Alphabet unit says that multiple pharmaceutical companies are already using IsoDDE to power drug discovery programs.

Pathogens such as viruses comprise numerous proteins that each power a different biological process. Drugs work by neutralizing a single, particularly important protein without which the pathogen can’t function. Developing a new drug requires researchers to find a vulnerable protein within a pathogen and then develop a compound that can effectively target it.

The first step of the workflow is mapping out the shape of a target protein. Researchers look for so-called binding pockets, recesses on the protein’s surface to which a drug can be attached. The task is highly complicated because proteins don’t have fixed shapes. Their configuration changes when they interact with other molecules or encounter new environmental conditions, which happens often.

Isomorphic says that IsoDDE speeds up the task of finding binding pockets. When there are no such pockets, it helps researchers develop compounds that cause a target protein to form them.

Once scientists identify a binding pocket, they have to find a way of attaching a drug molecule to it. The pharmaceutical industry searches for such binding mechanisms using a method called FEP. FEP algorithms can be highly hardware-intensive, which makes them costly. Moreover, they often require a detailed, three-dimensional model of a target protein.

The process of creating 3D protein models for FEP algorithms is itself a highly complex task. It requires scientists to freeze a target protein in a crystal and scan it using specialized X-ray equipment.

IsoDDE skips that step of the research workflow. Furthermore, Isomorphic

summary.tldr:
Alphabet’s Isomorphic Labs has secured $5 billion in a new funding round led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, with additional participation from Alphabet Inc. via its GV and CapitalG funds. The company, led by CEO Demis Hassabis, develops the Isomorphic Labs Drug Design Engine (IsoDDE), an AI-driven platform designed to accelerate pharmaceutical research by automating complex protein analysis and drug-target identification tasks.

IsoDDE aims to replace traditional, hardware-intensive methods like Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) algorithms, which typically require high-resolution 3D protein models derived from labor-intensive X-ray crystallography. The engine identifies binding pockets on protein surfaces and can induce the formation of such pockets where they do not naturally exist. Isomorphic claims the platform produces higher-quality output than FEP-based workflows with greater speed and precision. The new capital will be used to build bioengineering infrastructure, advance foundational biology models, and move the company's internal therapeutic programs toward clinical trials.
takeaways: **Funding:** Isomorphic Labs raised $5 billion in a round led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, with significant investment from parent company Alphabet.
**Core Technology:** The Isomorphic Labs Drug Design Engine (IsoDDE) automates the identification of protein binding pockets and drug-target compound development.
**Workflow Efficiency:** IsoDDE eliminates the need for X-ray crystallography-based 3D protein modeling, a prerequisite for traditional FEP (Free Energy Perturbation) algorithms.
**Strategic Goals:** The company plans to utilize the funding to scale its partner ecosystem, expand bioengineering infrastructure, and progress internal therapeutic programs to clinical trials.

title: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
author: Nilay Patel
contentSnippet: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it. “I am AGI-pilled in the sense that at an economy level, what is the political economy’s organization around AGI?” he asked at a roundtable discussion following his Microsoft Ignite keynote at the Chase Center in San Francisco. But Nadella doesn’t think frontier models like Claude are conscious. “I don’t think so,” he said, adding that he follows Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s view that companies should not give rights to models and treat them like they might have a moral status, which companies like Anthropic do as a matter of principle. Suleyman has told me he thinks Anthropic’s team has “wireheaded” themselves, and that this approach is dangerous. Nadella wasn’t quite as firm about it. “It’s a good debate,” he said. “I’m not sort of dogmatic about it. What I’m saying is the most important social technical issue we have to deal with is how do you ensure that an economy can diffuse this technology broadly?” I asked Nadella how he was thinking about AI after hearing his response to another reporter’s questions about Anthropic releasing more products in its office suite. Nadella talked at length about the potential collapse of the economy and the end of democracy if one AI model were allowed to achieve monopoly status. “Most people think about this as a competition between tech firms, which of course it will be,” he said. “But remember, the model has no limits. It’ll be a healthcare company. It can be a financial services company. It can be anything if it wants to be. It can take over the government. Thinking of this as some narrow competition between tech firms, of who is going to get to the next trillion dollars of market cap, is one of the strangest, narrowest ways to think about it.” Nadella went on to say that the very nature of companies stood to be disrupted in the future. “If intelligence has network effects, what is the future of a firm?” he asked. “If the model sees anything and learns it, and essentially all of human capital collapses into token capital, what is the role of a firm and the human capital in a firm? That’s the debate.” “I think the political economy is going to get more and more interesting in that context. No one — at least in a democracy — can

summary.tldr:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, speaking at a roundtable following the Microsoft Ignite keynote in San Francisco, articulated a shift in his perspective on Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), focusing on its systemic impact on political economy rather than the technical definition of consciousness. Nadella explicitly rejected the notion that frontier models like Anthropic’s Claude possess consciousness or moral status, aligning with Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s stance against granting rights to AI systems. He characterized the current discourse surrounding AI as overly focused on narrow competition between tech firms for market capitalization, arguing instead that the true risk lies in the potential for AI to disrupt the fundamental structure of firms, labor, and democratic governance.

Nadella posited that if intelligence exhibits network effects, the traditional concept of a firm may collapse as human capital is subsumed into 'token capital.' He warned that a monopolistic AI outcome—where a single entity controls the primary intelligence infrastructure—would be incompatible with democratic processes and economic stability. To counter this, Nadella emphasized Microsoft’s strategy of promoting a multi-model ecosystem, allowing enterprise clients to select cost-effective models and maintain data sovereignty. He argued that for a diverse economy to persist, the market must support a wide array of models rather than consolidating power into one or two dominant firms.
takeaways: **AGI Stance:** Satya Nadella defines his 'AGI-pilled' status as a concern for the political economy and the structural organization of society rather than a belief in model consciousness.

**Moral Status:** Nadella and Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman oppose granting moral status or rights to AI models, explicitly distancing themselves from the principles held by companies like Anthropic.

**Economic Risk:** Nadella warned that if AI models achieve monopoly status, they could effectively replace traditional firms, potentially leading to the collapse of labor markets and democratic election integrity.

**Strategic Counter-Measure:** Microsoft is positioning its AI platform to support a multi-model, sovereign-data approach to prevent the centralization of intelligence and ensure the survival of a diverse corporate landscape.

title: Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster
author: Tim Fernholz
contentSnippet:
Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.

China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an important topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week. The disclosure comes the same day Nvidia announced it was creating a board-level committee to oversee national security policies , export control compliance, and global trade risks.

Nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump. The arrangement required the chips to be shipped through the U.S., allowing the government to collect a 25% tariff.

The pathway angered China hawks who wanted to deny Chinese labs computing power and maintain the United States’ lead in AI, but Huang long argued that it was more important for the U.S. to compete in China. In April, he told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that “to concede that market for the United States technology industry is a disservice to our country.”

Huang’s ouster — in part over an affair with the CEO of a company under investigation for smuggling chips into China — has coincided with new rules, issued Monday, barring advanced U.S. chips from foreign data centers that serve Chinese customers remotely.

Investment bank Jefferies forecast that those rules might trim between $44 billion and $62 billion from Nvidia’s data center revenue next year. Referencing the new export controls, Kress said that the backlog of demand for advanced chips like Vera Rubin means the rules would have no impact on the company’s top-line revenue.

In the long term, the company may face the loss of potential customers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia. Critics of Nvidia’s dependence on China claim that as much as 20% of its revenue comes from demand linked to the country — annual revenue at its Singapore subsidiary hit $104 billion in 2025 before Nvidia stopped disclosing those figures — but that’s clearly going to change.

Even before Nvidia decided to stop shipping H200s, China had largely refused to accept their delivery. The government would prefer to generate demand for the country’s domestic chip industry, even if major AI compute users want the still-superior Nvidia equipment, according to Jacob Fe

summary.tldr:
Nvidia has officially ceased the sale of H200 chips to China, marking the end of a controversial export loophole that previously allowed shipments via the U.S. subject to a 25% tariff. This policy shift follows the departure of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, whose exit was reportedly linked to an affair with the CEO of a firm under investigation for chip smuggling. In response to the evolving regulatory landscape, Nvidia has established a board-level committee dedicated to national security, export compliance, and global trade risk management.

New U.S. export rules, issued Monday, now prohibit the sale of advanced chips to foreign data centers that provide services to Chinese customers. While investment bank Jefferies projected a potential $44 billion to $62 billion hit to Nvidia’s data center revenue, acting CEO Colette Kress stated that high demand for next-generation hardware like the Vera Rubin architecture will offset these losses. The new regulations also threaten Nvidia’s market share in Southeast Asian nations like Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia, as data centers in these regions must now certify they do not serve Chinese clients to remain eligible for Nvidia hardware.
takeaways: **Export Policy Shift:** Nvidia is terminating the sale of H200 chips to China, ending a deal previously brokered by Jensen Huang and Donald Trump that included a 25% U.S. tariff.

**Revenue Impact Forecast:** Jefferies estimates a $44 billion to $62 billion revenue reduction for Nvidia's data center segment, though acting CEO Colette Kress claims the Vera Rubin backlog will neutralize this impact.
**New Regulatory Constraints:** Recent rules bar the export of advanced chips to any foreign data center that provides remote access or services to Chinese customers.
**Compliance Requirements:** Data centers must now provide formal certification that they do not serve Chinese customers to purchase Nvidia hardware, or risk losing access to the company's products.
**Market Exposure:** Critics estimate that up to 20% of Nvidia's revenue is linked to Chinese demand, with the company's Singapore subsidiary reporting $104 billion in annual revenue in 2025.

title: Managed NVIDIA Dynamo on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference
author: Vinay Arora
contentSnippet: Serving large language models (LLMs) efficiently requires sufficient GPU memory and careful coordination of prompt processing and token generation. GLM-5.3’s FP8 weights, for example, exceed the 640 GB of GPU memory on a single ml.p5.48xlarge instance, before accounting for KV cache and runtime overhead. Long prompts can also slow token generation when both share the same GPUs. Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference now supports NVIDIA Dynamo , combining Dynamo’s distributed inference capabilities with the infrastructure management of HyperPod to address these challenges. Dynamo is an open source distributed inference framework that supports multi-node deployment, disaggregated prefill and decode, and KV-aware routing with engines such as vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM. HyperPod supports these deployments with high-performance Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking, coordinated GPU scheduling, and node health monitoring and recovery. In this post, we illustrate multi-node and disaggregated serving through a deployment example, share benchmark results, and outline best practices for optimizing inference on HyperPod. How the integration works The HyperPod Inference add-on installs the Dynamo custom resource definitions and these serving and scheduling components: HyperPod Inference Operator manages endpoint deployment through an InferenceEndpointConfig (IEC) custom resource. Its dynamoSpec section supplies the Dynamo configuration. Dynamo operator manages resources defined in a DynamoGraphDeployment (DGD) , including the frontend, model workers, replica counts, and resource requirements. Grove coordinates related groups of pods, including multi-node workers, and their scaling relationships. Kubernetes AI (KAI) Scheduler places pods on GPU resources, using gang scheduling to schedule the pods required for a multi-node worker together. AWS Deep Learning Containers (DLCs) provide the Dynamo runtime, while the add-on manages integrated component versions. To adopt a supported Dynamo release, update the add-on. Deployment architecture The following diagram shows the deployment paths, serving components, and infrastructure management for disaggregated inference on SageMaker HyperPod. The Dynamo frontend routes requests to prefill workers, which process prompts, and decode workers, which generate tokens. These separate pools allow independent scaling and tuning. Both p

summary.tldr:
Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference has integrated NVIDIA Dynamo, an open-source distributed inference framework, to facilitate the deployment of large language models (LLMs) that exceed the memory capacity of single instances. For instance, models like GLM-5.3 with FP8 weights surpass the 640 GB memory limit of an ml.p5.48xlarge instance when accounting for KV cache and runtime overhead. The integration leverages HyperPod’s infrastructure—including Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking, coordinated GPU scheduling, and automated node health monitoring—to support multi-node deployments and disaggregated inference architectures.

The architecture utilizes the HyperPod Inference Operator to manage endpoints via InferenceEndpointConfig (IEC) and DynamoGraphDeployment (DGD) resources. Key components include the Dynamo operator for managing model workers and replica counts, Grove for coordinating multi-node scaling, and the Kubernetes AI (KAI) Scheduler, which employs gang scheduling to ensure multi-node workers are placed on GPU resources simultaneously. The system supports engines such as vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM, allowing for disaggregated prefill and decode operations where separate worker pools process prompts and generate tokens independently.
takeaways: **Hardware Constraint:** A single ml.p5.48xlarge instance provides 640 GB of GPU memory, which is insufficient for models like GLM-5.3 in FP8 precision when including KV cache and runtime overhead.
**Architecture Components:** The integration uses the HyperPod Inference Operator, Dynamo operator, Grove for pod coordination, and the KAI Scheduler for gang scheduling.
**Supported Engines:** The Dynamo framework within HyperPod supports vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM for distributed inference.
**Disaggregated Serving:** The system enables independent scaling of prefill workers (prompt processing) and decode workers (token generation) to optimize performance for long prompts.

title: Nvidia says its open source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit
author: Sarah Perez
contentSnippet:
Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress reaffirmed the company’s commitment to open source AI during Tuesday’s earnings call with analysts — the first since CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation.

“At Nvidia, we are committed to fostering a vibrant open model ecosystem, so every country, company, and industry can build its own intelligence,” Kress said in her opening remarks. She also noted that open models were accelerating AI adoption, citing a 35-fold year-over-year surge in weekly token volume on OpenRouter, including a 3.5-fold increase over the past three months.

His departure had raised questions about the company’s future approach to open source AI models, with Hugging Face’s CEO calling Huang’s departure “a sad day,” and promising to “keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever.”

So far, Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face appear unchanged. The acquisition was not directly addressed during the Q&A portion of the earnings call.

“Together, we will scale its platform and make intelligence more open, more capable, and more accessible,” said Kress of Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face.

Last week, Nvidia founder Huang resigned from his position as CEO following news about his extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. He’s also accused of having extramarital affairs with two direct reports and is now set to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving. Meanwhile, the SEC is investigating Nvidia over whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, The WSJ reported .

Within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads. On today’s call, Kress noted that Nemotron is now the “most widely used U.S. open model on OpenRouter,” and it’s “where developers start to build their own intelligence.”

“That foundation is empowering the ecosystem,”

summary.tldr:
Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress confirmed that the company’s open-source AI strategy remains unchanged following the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang. During the company’s latest earnings call, Kress emphasized a continued commitment to fostering an open model ecosystem, citing a 35-fold year-over-year increase in weekly token volume on OpenRouter. takeaways: **Acquisition Status:** Nvidia’s $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face is proceeding as planned, marking the second-largest acquisition in the company's history.
**Model Performance:** The Nemotron model family is currently the most widely used U.S. open model on the OpenRouter platform.
**Market Growth:** Weekly token volume on OpenRouter has seen a 35-fold year-over-year increase, with a 3.5-fold growth observed in the last three months alone.
